channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: De olho nas eleições
item.description: O repórter Daniel Carvalho conta como Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula chegam antes do segundo turno das eleições. Com produção de Mariana Lumy e edição de Raphael Almeida. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Gold Steadies as Traders Assess US-Iran Tensions, Fed Rate Path
item.description: Gold was steady after rising moderately the previous day, as traders assessed Middle East tensions following President Donald Trump’s comments that the US wouldn’t attack Iran before November midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Yihui Xie

item.title: Chinese Bonds Become Source of Cheap Money for Global Borrowers
item.description: China is letting a wave of cheap money flow across its borders, turning the country into a rare source of low-cost funding for foreign borrowers.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Japan’s Household Spending Falls Again Despite Wage Gains
item.description: Japan’s household spending fell for a ninth month even as wages continued to climb, showing consumers remain cautious as persistent inflation squeezes purchasing power.
item.dc:creator: Yoshiaki Nohara

item.title: AI Debt Spree Hammers Tech Debt as Traders Rush to Reprice Risk
item.description: The rush to finance AI is rattling investors in the more than $10 trillion US corporate market, sparking a repricing of risks around some of the biggest technology companies that’s showing up in spiking prices for credit insurance, heightened volatility and weakening preformance.
item.dc:creator: Caleb Mutua, Preeti Singh and Laura Benitez

item.title: Barclays’ Lauren Lieberman on PepsiCo Earnings
item.description: Barclays US Equity Research Analyst Lauren Lieberman said PepsiCo’s positive share-price reaction was less a sign of broad optimism than a rebound after a period of weakness. She viewed the company’s acknowledgment that the status quo is not working—and that changes are needed—as the day’s biggest surprise, while its lowered full-year expectations were widely anticipated. She speaks with Romaine Bostick & Jess Menton on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Asian Stocks Drop on Tech Jitters, Oil Edges Lower: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks dropped, tracking declines on Wall Street, as speculation about OpenAI’s revenue revived concerns over the sustainability of the artificial-intelligence spending boom. Oil edged lower.
item.dc:creator: Toby Alder

item.title: True Religion CEO on Company Transformation and Gen Z Customers
item.description: True Religion CEO Michael Buckley discusses the brands comeback, noting its origins as a premium women’s denim brand in the early 2000s and its recent pivot toward more affordable offerings. Gen Z interest and attention from celebrities have helped revive the brand. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 9
item.description: Oil declined after President Donald Trump said that the US would not attack Iran ahead of November’s midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Rong Wei Neo and Kanoko Matsuyama

item.title: Rachel Gamarski conta sobre os cotados de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description:
Rachel Gamarski conta sobre os cotados para comandar a economia em um eventual governo de Flávio Bolsonaro. Com produção de Catarina Bacci e Patricia Xavier e edição de Mariana Lumy
(Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Patagonia CEO: Insist on Growing at Own Pace
item.description: Patagonia CEO Ryan Gellert, discusses the company’s approach to environmental activism, Gellert’s views on growth and profitability, and where he believes leaders across the industry stand. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Arc’teryx CEO on Product Expansion & Consumer Demand
item.description: Stuart Haselden CEO of Arc'teryx discusses the company's aims to nearly double revenue over the next five years by building on two strategic priorities. The company has focused on technical innovation and performance products, while divesting lifestyle products it believed diluted its brand authority. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fixed Income Leaders Dialogue
item.description: The fixed income landscape is evolving as public and private credit converge, AI-related financing accelerates and investors navigate a more complex credit cycle. TCW CIO of Fixed Income Bryan Whalen and Blackstone Credit & Insurance’s Philip Sherrill were in conversation with Bloomberg’s Scarlet Fu at the Bloomberg Future of Fixed Income 2026 conference in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Chipotle Jumps on Report Starbucks Has Explored Takeover
item.description:
Shares of Chipotle Mexican Grill jumped after the Financial Times reported that Starbucks Corp. has worked with advisers in recent months on a takeover proposal for the burrito chain.
The status of the takeover plans couldn’t be immediately learned and a mega deal of this size might never get off the ground, the FT said, citing people familiar with the matter. Brian Niccol, Starbucks’ chief executive officer since 2024, previously spent six years as the top executive at Chipotle, where he spearheaded a period of rapid growth.
For more, we speak with Redd Brown, Bloomberg News Consumer Reporter. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Bond ETFs Are Reshaping Portfolio Construction
item.description: Bond ETFs are moving into their next phase, with active strategies, new product structures and more specialized exposures changing how investors build fixed income portfolios. State Street Investment Management’s Ethan Balakier, BondBloxx’s Joanna Gallegos and Schwab Asset Management’s Riz Hussain joined Bloomberg Intelligence’s Eric Balchunas at the Bloomberg Future of Fixed Income 2026 conference in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Global Banks Bolster Japan Debt Teams as Bond Issuance Booms
item.description: Global financial institutions are beefing up their debt capital market teams in Japan, hiring bankers and relocating staff, to capture a boom in fundraising driven by mergers, acquisitions, and artificial intelligence capital.
item.dc:creator: Atsuko Fukase

item.title: Firmus Misfire Casts Shadow on Data Center IPOs in the Pipeline
item.description: The expected postponement of Nvidia Corp.-backed data center company Firmus Grid Ltd.’s Australian IPO is an ominous sign for other proposed listings, coming after a string of disappointing debuts for artificial intelligence infrastructure firms.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Hughes

item.title: Brazil Election: Bolsonaro Says He’d Work With US, China as President
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro said he would work with the US and China if he becomes Brazil’s president, after a surprise election performance left him poised to join a wave of conservative leaders pushing Latin America closer to Washington.
item.dc:creator: Augusta Saraiva and Daniel Carvalho

item.title: Gold Rises After Trump Says US Won’t Attack Iran Before Midterms
item.description: Gold rose from a two-month low, with traders assessing the outlook for energy prices after President Donald Trump said the US won’t attack Iran before the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Sybilla Gross and Jack Ryan

item.title: Ray Dalio Warns of US Debt Crisis Within Three Years
item.description: Bridgewater Associates Founder Ray Dalio warns that the US is approaching the limits of its debt cycle, predicting a potential crisis within three years as spending outpaces revenue. He cautions that rising borrowing costs and weakening demand from key foreign buyers may squeeze lower-income borrowers first. (Source: Bloomberg)
